# Retire the dead `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` harness

## Problem statement

`tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` (567 lines) asserts fast/cheap operating-mode
selection by extracting fixtures from `proxy/config-fast.yaml` and
`proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — files deleted by LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA
(priority-based routing replaced the mode axis). The harness now aborts in
fixture setup (`FileNotFoundError` → `0 passed, 1 failed`) before any
assertion runs, and because no pytest wrapper or CI job collects it, the
rot is invisible to the default suite: it gives a false sense of mode
coverage while validating nothing.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / producer (Richard)** — needs the test tree to contain only
  harnesses that can fail meaningfully; a permanently red, uncollected harness
  wastes triage time (three near-identical work items were filed for it:
  LP-0MVFJQAID007YB0H, LP-0MVKD0P7R002D5L8, this one).
- **Future implementation agents** — need an honest coverage map of
  `start-proxy.sh` so they do not re-add coverage that already exists in
  pytest.

### Example user story

- As an agent asked to change `start-proxy.sh`, I can run the documented
  harnesses and trust that a green result means something, rather than
  triaging a harness whose only failure is a missing file it does not own.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Harness removed.** `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` no longer
  exists (`git rm`), with the commit message recording why: the fast/cheap
  mode axis was removed by LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA, and every surviving assertion
  is either dead or already covered (see **Existing state** coverage matrix).
- [ ] **AC2 — Reference sweep.** A repo-wide sweep (excluding `.worklog/`)
  shows no test, harness or CI job **loads** `proxy/config-fast.yaml` or
  `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`. The only remaining textual mentions
  (`tests/test_mode_flip_analysis.py` log fixtures) are either removed or
  carry a one-line comment marking them as historical log data. The sweep
  command and its result are recorded in a work-item comment.
- [ ] **AC3 — Sibling harnesses still green.** `tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh`,
  `tests/test_start_proxy_detach.sh` (and its `tests/test_start_proxy_detach_shell.py`
  wrapper), `tests/test_start_proxy_launch_modes.py` and
  `tests/test_start_proxy_restart.sh` (documented `LIVE_PORT_KILL_TESTS=1`
  opt-in) all still pass after the change.
- [ ] **AC4 — Documentation touch-points verified.** `docs/INTEGRATION.md`
  (shell-harness table) remains accurate; no doc, skill, README, CI workflow
  or pytest wrapper references the deleted harness (current sweep finds none —
  re-verify and update if the picture changed).
- [ ] **AC5 — Suite and docs.** The full project test suite passes with the
  changes (run through the test skill / dev-push gate), and all related
  documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments,
  README, and any relevant docs entries.

## Constraints

- Do **not** reinstate per-mode configs or revive a mode API — the mode axis is
  deliberately gone (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA).
- **Scope is this harness + the reference sweep + doc verification only.** Other
  mode-era residue stays untouched in this item and is tracked separately
  (`discovered-from:` follow-ups): `.gitignore` lines 50–55 (`proxy/.mode*`),
  the untracked runtime file `proxy/.mode`, `scripts/analyze_mode_flips.py`,
  `docs/mode-flip-analysis-LP-0MV9UNE75004903J.md`, and the
  `tests/test_mode_flip_analysis.py` module (historical log analysis — only its
  fixture strings are annotated, not retired).
- Do not weaken assertions in the three live start-proxy harnesses; they must
  keep passing unchanged.
- Worktree isolation and build → test → commit ordering per the implement skill.

## Existing state

Reproduction on the `dev` tip (2026-10-25):

```
$ bash tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh
FileNotFoundError: ... '/home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/config-fast.yaml'
FAIL: could not extract mode-relevant values from real configs (cheap slots= ctx=; fast slots= ctx=)
=== Results: 0 passed, 1 failed ===
```

`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` has no mode surface left: `CONFIG_FILE` is
hard-coded to `$REPO_ROOT/config.yaml` (lines 368–369), there is no `.mode`
read, `LLAMA_PROXY_CONFIG` is never exported (0 occurrences), and the launcher
detaches by default, so the harness's fake-`python3` interception of the final
`exec uvicorn` only works because LP-0MVK3KIPZ002SR32 patched in
`--foreground` (commit `0a3a6023`) — a mechanical fix that left the dead
assertions in place.

### Coverage matrix — what the harness asserted vs. what covers it today

| Harness test | Asserted | Status today |
|---|---|---|
| `test_cheap_mode`, `test_fast_mode`, `test_missing_mode`, `test_missing_mode_config_fallback`, `test_invalid_mode` | `.mode` selects/rejects an overlay and exports `LLAMA_PROXY_CONFIG` | **Dead** — no `.mode`, no `LLAMA_PROXY_CONFIG`, no overlays; `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py::test_config_overlays_gone` pins their absence |
| `test_api_keys_resolve_from_selected_config` | the unselected profile's keys are not required | **Dead as written** (mode-driven); live coverage: `tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh` Tests 1–7 |
| `test_api_keys_from_merged_base` | `api_key_env` declared in the base config is still detected | **Live behaviour** (`load_merged` at `start-proxy.sh:384–405`); covered by `tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh` Test 6 and `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` |
| `test_per_slot_context` | echoed `FAKE_MODE_FACTS` equals 83285 (cheap) / 258048 (fast) | **Dead** — expected values derived from the deleted overlays; the formula is unit-tested via `provider.effective_per_slot_threshold`, and `test_slot_pool_fixed_at_2` pins today's slot count |
| `test_web_ui_slots_text` | `index.html` contains `"<N>-slot local pool"` (mode-era cheap capacity text) | **Dead** — that text no longer exists in `proxy/templates/index.html` |
| `test_restart_preserves_unchanged_merged_config`, `test_restart_on_base_only_change`, `test_restart_on_overlay_only_change` | merged-config signature stability / invalidation through `--restart` | **Overlay half dead** (no overlays); merged-signature contract covered by `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` (`merged_config_sha256` suite) and `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py::test_config_file_sha256_hashes_merged_not_raw_overlay` / `..._matches_shared_merged_helper`; the sandbox fixture also writes a stale signature schema (`"mode"` field; `lifecycle._write_llama_server_signature` no longer takes a mode) |

## Desired change

1. Delete `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` (`git rm`), with a commit message
   that names the removed feature and points at the surviving coverage.
2. Sweep for references to the removed mode configs and annotate the historical
   log fixtures in `tests/test_mode_flip_analysis.py` (or remove those strings
   if the producer prefers) — no config *loading* may remain.
3. Re-verify the documentation touch-points listed in AC4 and update
   `docs/INTEGRATION.md` only if it has drifted.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` — the dead harness; delete it.
- `tests/test_mode_flip_analysis.py` — only remaining textual mentions of
  `config-fast.yaml` (historical log-line fixtures); annotate as historical.
- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — read-only reference: single-config
  resolution, detach-by-default launch; no mode handling remains.
- `docs/INTEGRATION.md` — shell-harness / opt-in test table; verify only.
- `proxy/tests/test_priority_routing.py` — `test_config_overlays_gone`,
  `test_slot_pool_fixed_at_2`: the pytest assertions that already guard the
  removed-mode invariants.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA** — priority-based routing replacing fast/cheap mode
  (removed the overlays, the `.mode` state and `proxy.mode`); root cause.
- **LP-0MVK3KIPZ002SR32** — detach-by-default launch; patched this harness with
  `--foreground` (commit `0a3a6023`) instead of retiring it.
- **LP-0MVK3KZ280076W93** — integration verification that surfaced the
  pre-existing failure.
- **LP-0MVFJQAID007YB0H** and **LP-0MVKD0P7R002D5L8** — near-identical
  duplicates of this defect, both claimed by live intake sessions when this
  brief was written; this item's ACs are the superset (they add the repo-wide
  sweep in AC2). See **Decisions** D3.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVFJQAID007YB0H** – tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh is stale: references removed config-fast.yaml / config-cheap.yaml (in-progress)
- **LP-0MN6JRADW0NL3E5W** – Remove systemd service files for llama-proxy (completed)
- **LP-0MRNV040H0055N2Q** – [test-failure] test_stub_router_integration — flaky test-ordering-dependent assert ok Failure (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: acceptance, anything, assert, assertion, asserts (+55 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: acceptance, anything, assert, assertion, asserts (+55 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: acceptance, anything, assert, assertion, asserts (+55 more)

## Risks, assumptions and failure modes

- **Assumption (producer may override):** deletion, not a rewrite, is the right
  fix. Evidence: the harness targets a removed surface, its remaining
  assertions are duplicated in pytest, and a faithful rewrite would be a new
  harness, not a repair. If the producer prefers a rewrite, AC1 becomes
  "rewritten harness runs green and asserts only live `start-proxy.sh`
  behaviour".
- **Failure mode — duplicate implementations:** three items describe this
  defect and two siblings are being intaken concurrently. Mitigation: comments
  record the duplication on both siblings; only one deletion commit is needed.
- **Failure mode — hidden consumer:** an out-of-repo job could invoke the

  `.sh`/`.py`/`.md` files (current sweep: no consumers).
- **Failure mode — perceived coverage loss:** deleting a harness can look like

- **Scope-creep risk:** mode-era residue (`.gitignore` mode entries,

## Decisions

- **D1 — Delete rather than rewrite.** Rationale as above; producer may

- **D2 — Keep `tests/test_mode_flip_analysis.py`.** It classifies historical
  log lines from before the mode removal; its `config-fast.yaml` strings are

discovered-from:LP-0MVJNIZRO008S031

## Summary

`.githooks/post-merge` and `.githooks/post-rewrite` `exec` a hard-coded path into a *different* checkout (`/home/rgardler/projects/llm-manager/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`) that does not exist on this host. Every `git pull`/`git merge`/`git rebase` in the main checkout therefore prints

```
.githooks/post-merge: 4: exec: /home/rgardler/projects/llm-manager/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found
```

and the post-pull Worklog sync silently does not run. The hook is fail-open, so pulls still succeed — which is exactly why the breakage went unnoticed.

## Problem statement

The two post-pull Worklog hooks are template files copied from the `llm-manager` project and still point back at that project's checkout. On this clone the target path is gone, so the hooks are dead weight that emit a shell error on every merge and skip the sync they exist to perform. The repo already commits its own copy of the target script at `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, so the delegation target simply needs to resolve repo-locally instead of to the template checkout.

## Users

- **Primary user — agent/operator pulling `dev` in the main checkout.** Wants a pull with clean output and a Worklog data branch that is actually synced afterwards.
- **Secondary user — future maintainer of this repo's hooks.** Wants one repo-owned implementation, not a pointer into an unrelated project that rots silently.

Example user stories:

- *As an agent pulling `dev` into the main checkout, I want the post-merge hook to run this repo's Worklog sync, so that worklog data brought in by the pull is synced without me doing it by hand.*
- *As an operator, I want no `exec: ... not found` on stderr during a pull, so that real errors are not buried in known noise.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the hook to resolve its delegate from the repo it lives in, so that the automation cannot silently die when another project moves or is deleted.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.githooks/post-merge` and `.githooks/post-rewrite` delegate to the repo-local `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` resolved from the repository root (no hard-coded `/home/rgardler/projects/llm-manager/...` path remains in either file).
- [ ] Running the hooks in a clean main checkout (`git merge --ff-only`, and a `git commit --amend`/rebase that triggers `post-rewrite`) emits no `exec: ... not found` and no other stderr noise introduced by the fix.
- [ ] The delegate really runs: hook arguments (`$@`) and, for `post-rewrite`, stdin are passed through to `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` unchanged.
- [ ] `tests/test_git_hooks.py` gains behavioural coverage that invokes the two hooks in its sandbox and asserts the repo-local delegate ran with the expected arguments and that stderr contains no "not found"; a hook pointing outside the sandbox must fail that test.
- [ ] `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check` still exits 0 with the hooks active, and the fix does not change hook installation behaviour.
- [ ] `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` is updated to state that `post-merge`/`post-rewrite` delegate to the repo-local `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` (hook matrix), and that the hook files are repo-owned and never point at another checkout.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Dependencies

None. Self-contained change to two committed hook files, their tests and one docs page.

## Constraints

- `.githooks/` files are committed hook files; `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh` must keep touching **only** `core.hooksPath` and executable bits — it must never generate, copy or rewrite hook content.
- Hooks must stay POSIX `sh` (they run as `#!/bin/sh`) and fail-open: a missing `wl`/`worklog` binary or an uninitialised `.worklog` must not fail a pull (existing behaviour, preserved).
- The existing skip guards must be preserved: `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1`, temp-worktree `$PWD` match, and linked-worktree detection (hooks are no-ops inside worktrees).
- No behaviour change to `.githooks/pre-push` (its gate is covered by existing tests and is out of scope).
- `sh` hooks are invoked by git with the working directory at the working-tree root for non-bare repos, so a repo-root-relative resolution is available (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`).

## Existing state

- `.githooks/post-merge` (4 lines) and `.githooks/post-rewrite` (4 lines) are identical thin wrappers: a v1 marker comment plus `exec "/home/rgardler/projects/llm-manager/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"`.
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` **already exists in this repo** (committed, executable, 1130 B) and contains the real sync logic. It is functionally a clone of `.githooks/post-checkout`, differing only in the version marker and the env-var name (`WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL` vs `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_CHECKOUT`).
- `/home/rgardler/projects/llm-manager` does not exist on this host; a copy of the same script survives at `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`.
- `core.hooksPath` is `.githooks` in this clone, so the broken wrappers do run (observed 2026-10-23 after fast-forwarding `dev` to `306c0219`).
- `tests/test_git_hooks.py` covers only `pre-push` and the installer; the post-* hooks have no coverage, which is why the stale path shipped unnoticed.
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` already lists `post-merge`, `post-rewrite`, `worklog-post-pull` in its hook matrix but does not say where the delegate lives.

## Desired change

Resolve the delegate from the repository the hook lives in, so the wrappers become:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# worklog:post-pull-hook:v2
# Delegate to this repository's Worklog post-pull sync script.
exec "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"
```

with the explanatory comment updated to say the script is repo-local (v2 marker so a stale v1 template copy is identifiable), plus the sandbox behavioural tests and the docs update described in the ACs.

### Decisions

- **Fix the path rather than delete the wrappers.** The AC allows removal "when that automation is not available in this repo", but it *is* available: `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is committed here. Removing the hooks would drop post-pull syncing, a behaviour regression.
- **No fallback to `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`.** A per-user global path would make hook behaviour host-dependent and reintroduce a silent cross-checkout dependency. The repo-local committed file is authoritative; a fallback chain would be speculative complexity.
- **No `-x` pre-check / custom error message.** The delegate is a committed sibling; the only way it vanishes is a corrupt checkout, where a plain shell exec error is already actionable. Keeps the wrapper minimal.
- **`post-checkout` deduplication is out of scope.** `.githooks/post-checkout` carries its own inline copy of the same ~30-line sync script. Folding it into the delegate would be a tidy-up, but it is a separate behavioural change (different skip env var) and not required to fix this defect; recorded here as an observation only.
- **Priority raised `low` → `medium`.** Per the priority guide, `low` is for polish with *no* functional impact; here a Worklog automation silently stops running, which is a functional (if non-blocking) defect.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/post-merge` — replace the hard-coded template path with a repo-root-relative resolution of the delegate; bump marker to `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2`.
- `.githooks/post-rewrite` — same change; confirm stdin is forwarded (it is, implicitly, via `exec`).
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — unchanged (the delegation target); read it to confirm the skip guards the tests must respect.
- `tests/test_git_hooks.py` — add sandbox behavioural tests: delegate invoked with the hook's args, stdin forwarded for `post-rewrite`, no `not found` on stderr, and a regression case proving a template-style absolute path fails the test.
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — hook matrix note that `post-merge`/`post-rewrite` delegate to the repo-local `worklog-post-pull`, and that hooks are repo-owned.

## Related work

Duplicate check performed (`wl search "githooks"`) — no completed item satisfies this item's ACs: the code is still broken today (`ls -d /home/rgardler/projects/llm-manager` → no such file), and the one candidate, LP-0MVLIJRCH006EIBM, was closed **as a duplicate of this item** with its fix guidance preserved as a comment here. No overlap requiring a rewrite.

- **LP-0MVLIJRCH006EIBM** — *Stale `.githooks/post-merge` path breaks every merge (points at llm-manager checkout)* (completed, closed as duplicate of this item). Same defect; it contributed the repo-root-relative fix and the `tests/test_git_hooks.py` verification guidance preserved as a comment here.
- **LP-0MVFFJWPW007ZEPK** — *Install the `.githooks/pre-push` gate (core.hooksPath)…* (completed). Introduced the committed-hooks model and `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`; that installer deliberately does not manage hook content, which is why the stale delegate must be fixed in the hook files themselves.
- **LP-0MVHSWUE80097KQJ** — *Pre-push full-suite gate not wired in this checkout (`core.hooksPath` unset)* (completed). Same activation surface as AC5 here.
- **LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8** — *Surface proxy-side compaction metadata in responses* (completed) — its notes record an earlier duplicate of this same class of breakage: `.githooks/post-checkout` then delegated to a missing `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`. Evidence that the inlined `post-checkout` script predates this defect's fix and that the wrappers were seeded from an external template.
- **LP-0MVJNIZRO008S031** — parent discovery item (the push whose fast-forward exposed the error).
- **LP-0MVLCMBBA00850WL** — *Remove stray tracked file named '=' at repo root* (open, unrelated) — noted only because it also touches `.githooks` verification guidance.
- `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — the hook matrix and install/verify contract this change must keep true.
- `tests/test_git_hooks.py` — the existing sandbox-based hook test harness the new tests extend.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — template resurfacing.** `.githooks/post-*` were seeded from the `llm-manager` template by hand; SorraAgents' installer does not ship them (verified: no `install_pi.sh`/`worklog-post-pull` reference). Mitigation: a v2 marker plus the new sandbox test fails loudly if a v1 template copy is re-introduced.
- **Risk — test brittleness.** Assertions must be behavioural (delegate invoked, args forwarded, stderr clean) *not* a grep of hook source; the sandbox must replace the delegate with a marker-writing fake so the real `wl sync` never runs in tests.
- **Risk — noisy test environments.** The real delegate prints sync warnings when `.worklog` is absent or `wl` fails, so tests must stub the delegate rather than assert on the real one's stderr.
- **Assumption.** `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` is available and correct inside these hooks (git runs non-bare hooks with cwd at the worktree root). Confirmed by reproducing the merge in a throwaway sandbox repo.
- **Scope-creep guard.** No changes to `pre-push`, to the installer's behaviour, or to the `post-checkout` inline script. Any further cleanup (deduplicating `post-checkout`, removing the global `~/.config/pi/.githooks/` copy, fixing the same template in other projects) is recorded as a linked work item, not folded in here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Is the automation available in this repo, or should the wrappers be removed?** — Answer (research, no user input needed): available. `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is committed and executable in this checkout (1130 B, `ls -l .githooks/`). Source: `ls -l .githooks/`, `cat .githooks/worklog-post-pull`. Therefore AC1 resolves to "fix the path", not "remove the wrapper".
- **Q: Does anything regenerate `.githooks/post-*` that would re-break the fix?** — Answer (research): no. `grep -rn worklog-post-pull` over `*.sh`/`*.py` finds no generator; `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh` only sets `core.hooksPath` and repairs exec bits; the SorraAgents installer has no reference to these hooks. Source: `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`, `grep` over the repo and `~/projects/SorraAgents`.
- **Q: Should the delegate fall back to the surviving `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` copy?** — Answer (research/decision): no. The copy exists (`ls -la ~/.config/pi/.githooks/`) but a per-user fallback makes behaviour host-dependent and hides a broken checkout. Source: `ls -la ~/.config/pi/.githooks`, `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` (repo-owned committed hooks).
- **Q: Does the failure reproduce, and is it fail-open?** — Answer (research): yes. Reproduced in a throwaway sandbox repo with this repo's hooks: `git merge` printed `.githooks/post-merge: 4: exec: …/llm-manager/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found` on stderr and still exited 0. Source: sandbox reproduction in `/tmp/hookrepro`; matches the observed 2026-10-23 report.
- **Q: Does `post-rewrite` need explicit stdin forwarding?** — Answer (research): no. The hook script receives the rewritten commits on stdin; `exec` inherits the file descriptor, so `"$@"` plus the inherited stdin is sufficient. Bug in the proxy-usage-analysis report (report.md, 'Local model utilization' notes), generated 2026-10-23 08:00 from /var/log/llama-proxy (window 2026-10-22 08:00 -> 2026-10-23 08:00).

The note reads: '1677 of 676 stream(s) contributed a measured prefill (a first-byte line); the rest fall back to their decode interval...' — a contributing count (1677) larger than the stream population it annotates (676 streams served in the window).

The per-phase tables are internally consistent: Prefill samples 727, Decode samples 725, Streams served 676. So '1677' is a counter/summing error in the note text, not a data problem.

**Root cause (verified 2026-10-24):** `BusyStats.prefill_extended_streams` is incremented for **every** paired stream in the margin-widened event collection (48h collection margin + 24h window), regardless of whether that pair's busy interval overlaps the report window. `BusyStats.streams` (the denominator '676') counts only paired streams whose clipped busy interval is non-empty inside the window (`intervals`). Streams from outside the window (earlier windows caught in the 48h margin) inflate the numerator (1677) far beyond the in-window population (676) — reproduced across several daily reports (1542 of 111, 1668 of 671, 1714 of 727, ...). The counter is incremented just above the `if b_hi > b_lo:` append in `compute_busy_stats`, so the fix is to increment it only for pairs whose interval is actually added (X <= Y then follows directly, and the same over-count in the JSON summary `prefill_extended_streams` key is fixed too).

Note: the Prefill table's Samples column (727) counts matched first-byte samples anchored in the window **including unfinished streams**, so it may legitimately exceed Streams served (676). The note counter is a different population (paired, in-window, dispatch-extended) and must stay <= Streams served — it may not equal the Samples count.

ACs:
1. The note's 'X of Y stream(s)' framing is corrected so X <= Y and consistent with the Prefill table's Samples column.
2. A regression test asserts the busy-accounting note counters are bounded by the streams-served count.
3. The report remains deterministic given the same logs (no drift when re-run).

**Key Files:**
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — `compute_busy_stats` increments `prefill_extended` for all paired streams incl. out-of-window pairs (bug site ~line 1069; fix next to the `b_hi > b_lo` append ~line 1093).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — note text rendered at line ~1362 ('X of Y stream(s) contributed a measured prefill'); JSON summary key at line ~2220.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — existing busy/prefill tests (~lines 3119-3315); home for the new regression test asserting `prefill_extended_streams <= streams`.

# Slot save/restore measurement harness — scaffolding, fixtures and offline tests

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE (virtual-slot spike). This is the tracer-bullet slice:
the reusable measurement core that every later measurement child drives.

## Target outcome

A committed, reproducible harness at
`proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py` that can (a) build prompts of
an exact token size, (b) drive llama-server's slot endpoints directly
(`POST /slots/{id}?action=save` / `?action=restore`), (c) issue a deterministic
completion and read llama.cpp's own `timings`, and (d) record failures instead of
retrying them away.

## Minimal implementation

- New module `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py` following the
  conventions of `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` (direct llama-server HTTP,
  `timings.prompt_n` / `prompt_ms` / `prompt_per_second`, percentile helper,
  salted unique prompts to defeat the slot prompt cache) and
  `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` (argparse, `--output-dir`, JSON results,
  `LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT`).
- Prompt fixtures for 38K / 72K / 100K / 124K tokens using the project's own
  tokenizer resolution (`proxy.provider._get_tokenizer_for_model`) so token
  counts are native Qwen3 counts, not char/4 guesses; a `--dry-run` mode that
  validates sizes without touching the GPU.
- Slot-endpoint client mirroring the proxy's real call shape
  (`proxy/proxy/session.py::_call_slot_endpoint`): `{"filename": <basename>}`
  payload, adaptive timeout, and a recorded outcome
  (`ok | http_error | timeout | exception`) with elapsed seconds — **no retry**.
- A result record schema (one row per attempt) written to
  `results/<run-label>/raw.json` plus a markdown renderer, so every later child
  only adds columns/measurements rather than new plumbing.
- Offline unit tests using a mocked llama-server (httpx `MockTransport` /
  respx) covering: request shape, timeout classification (ReadTimeout recorded,
  not retried), non-200 recording, restore-skipped-when-file-missing, and
  `prompt_n`/`cached_tokens` derivation including the zero-prefill (full cache
  hit) case.
- A guard test asserting the harness imports no production runtime module that
  changes proxy behaviour (only read-only helpers), i.e. AC5 of the spike is
  structurally protected.
- README subsection under `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` documenting fixtures,
  driver, environment variables and the validity caveats inherited from
  `docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py` exists, is importable, and
  `--help` / `--dry-run` work with no live llama-server.
- `--dry-run` reports the exact native token count for each of 38K / 72K / 100K
  / 124K and fails loudly when a fixture cannot reach its target size.
- Unit tests cover the five behaviours listed above and pass offline (no GPU,
  no network).
- Every attempt row records `outcome`, `elapsed_s`, `timeout_s`, `slot_id`,
  `filename` and (when the request ran) `prompt_n`, `prompt_total`,
  `cached_tokens`, `cached_ratio`.
- A failure (timeout / non-200 / exception) is recorded as a row and the run
  continues — verified by a test that asserts no retry occurs.
- The guard test proves the harness does not import production request-path
  modules.
- `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` documents usage, fixtures and caveats.

## Constraints

- No production behaviour change: nothing under `proxy/proxy/` may be modified.
- Runs must be safe to abort: each request carries an explicit timeout and the
  harness never issues a second save/restore for the same slot concurrently
  (llama-server serialises KV copies).
- Results are append-only artifacts under `proxy/benchmarks/results/`.

## Risky assumptions

- llama-server's slot save/restore endpoint responds with an echoing body
  (`n_saved` / `n_restored`); if it does not, the hit signal must come from
  `timings.prompt_n` plus the llama-server log (`prompt_save: ... length N`).
  The harness must therefore support both signals rather than assuming one.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py` (new)
- `proxy/benchmarks/README.md`
- `proxy/tests/benchmarks/test_slot_save_restore_benchmark.py` (new)
- `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` (reference pattern)
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` (reference: `_call_slot_endpoint` call shape)
- `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py` (reference)
data.title: Slot save/restore measurement harness: scaffolding, fixtures, offline tests

# Measure slot save cost: wall time, on-disk size, success rate

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 1 of the spike.

## Target outcome

A measured table of `slot save` cost for prompt sizes 38K / 72K / 100K / 124K
tokens: wall-clock time, on-disk snapshot size, bytes per token, and success
rate — including the intermittent ReadTimeout failures, which must be counted,
not retried away.

## Minimal implementation

- Measurement mode in `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
  (`--mode save --sizes 38000,72000,100000,124000 --reps N`).
- Per repetition: unique salted prompt → completion to force a real prefill into
  the slot → `POST /slots/{id}?action=save` → record elapsed, status, on-disk
  `stat().st_size` of the snapshot, plus the llama-server log's own
  `prompt_save: - saving prompt with length N, total state size = X MiB` line for
  cross-validation.
- Derive bytes/token = size / prompt_n and compare with the profile's physical
  KV-per-token expectation from `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py`.
- Emit `results/<label>/save.json` + a markdown table with per-size
  p50 / p90 / max save seconds and success rate; failures broken out by
  outcome class (`timeout`, `http_error`, `exception`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Results table covering all four prompt sizes with, per size: n attempts,
  success rate, save wall time p50/p90/max, snapshot size, bytes/token.
- Observed failure rate and failure classes recorded explicitly; if zero failures
  occur the report states the sample size and the window's historical rate
  (`slot_save failed` count) instead of implying saves are reliable.
- The llama-server log's `total state size` agrees with the on-disk size within
  5%, or the discrepancy is reported with an explanation.
- Repeated runs are reproducible: re-running with the same `--sizes`/`--reps`
  produces a new timestamped result directory and does not overwrite prior
  results.
- The run is safe to interrupt and leaves no snapshot it did not record
  (cleanup of its own files listed in the results).

## Constraints

- Save must be issued only when the slot is otherwise idle; concurrent saves are
  serialised by llama-server and would inflate the timing.
- Snapshot files are large (~0.5-0.7 GiB each) — the run must cap total bytes
  written and clean up after itself via `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`
  semantics, without touching snapshots it did not create.

## Risks

- The `session_slot_skip_when_busy` production gate does not exist in this
  harness path, so saves will be issued under whatever load exists; the run must
  record competing local activity (proxy `local_dispatch_records`) per attempt.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/save.json` (new artifact)
- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`
- `docs/slot-persistence-analysis-harness.md` (evidence schema reference)

# Measure restore cost and restore hit-rate (the core spike question)

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 2 — this is the load-bearing question:
does a restore actually avoid re-prefill, and how much does it cost?

## Target outcome

For each prompt size (38K / 72K / 100K / 124K), a paired comparison between
(a) a **cold** run — fresh slot, no snapshot, full prefill — and (b) a
**restored** run — save, evict/clear the slot, restore, then replay the same
prompt — reporting time-to-first-token, tokens actually evaluated
(`timings.prompt_n`), tokens reused from cache, and the resulting hit-rate.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode restore` in the harness: for each size and repetition run the pair
  `cold` then `save → clear slot → restore → replay` and record both rows.
- Hit is derived from tokens, not wall time: `cached_tokens = prompt_total -
  timings.prompt_n`, `cached_ratio = cached_tokens / prompt_total`. A run is a
  **hit** when `cached_ratio >= --hit-threshold` (default 0.9); a run is a
  **miss** when the restore returned OK but `prompt_n` shows a full re-prefill.
  Latency is reported alongside, never used as the primary hit definition.
- Report per size: cold prefill seconds (p50), restored first-byte seconds (p50),
  speed-up factor, hit-rate, and miss/partial-hit distribution.
- Cross-check against the llama-server log (restored-checkpoint lines / full
  re-processing markers) and against `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`
  from the completion response, recording any disagreement.
- `results/<label>/restore.json` + markdown table; the JSON must be directly
  consumable by the break-even model in the verdict child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Paired cold-vs-restored table for all four sizes, n >= 3 per cell, with
  per-size: cold TTFT p50, restored TTFT p50, speed-up, hit-rate, and the
  distribution of `cached_ratio`.
- The hit definition (`cached_ratio >= threshold`) is documented in the results
  output and the doc, and both the token-based and latency-based views are
  reported so the verdict can cite either.
- Partial hits are reported distinctly from full misses (a 40% prefix reuse is
  not a "miss").
- Any disagreement between `timings.prompt_n`, the response
  `cached_tokens`, and the llama-server log markers is reported, not silently
  reconciled.
- The cold baseline for each size is measured in the same run and window as its
  restored pair, so no cross-run drift is attributed to restore.
- Results are reproducible (timestamped result dir; salt recorded so the same
  prompts can be regenerated).

## Constraints

- The restore must be issued into a slot that does not already hold the same
  prefix, otherwise the measurement proves nothing — the harness must clear or
  overwrite the slot between save and restore and assert that it did.

## Risks

- If llama-server refuses to restore a snapshot for a hybrid-attention model, the
  failure will surface as either an explicit non-200 or a silent full re-prefill.
  The harness must distinguish these (this is the difference between "restore is
  broken" and "restore is ignored").

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/restore.json` (new artifact)
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` (`_restore_slot_snapshot` semantics)
- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` (cached-token derivation reference)
data.title: Measure restore cost and restore hit-rate (cold vs restored, paired)

# Characterise restored-cache invalidation (hybrid-attention behaviour)

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 3.

## Target outcome

Quantified answer to the hypothesis risk in the parent: this build is Qwen3.x
hybrid attention + recurrent/SWA, and llama.cpp already invalidates its own
context checkpoints, so a restored snapshot may be rejected or only partially
usable. Produce a measured invalidation rate by *reuse shape*, plus the tokens
re-processed as a result.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode invalidation` in the harness, driving four restore shapes per size:
  1. exact replay — same prompt, no extension (best case);
  2. one-turn extension — same prompt + a short follow-up user turn (the real
     session pattern);
  3. prefix drift — same prompt with a modified system-prompt head (should
     always miss, guards against over-crediting);
  4. cold control — no snapshot at all.
- Parse llama-server log markers between requests: `forcing full prompt
  re-processing`, `erased invalidated context checkpoint ... n_swa`,
  `restored context checkpoint`, and `n_past = ... slot.prompt.tokens.size()`.
  Attribute markers to an attempt by slot id + log offset captured immediately
  before and after each request.
- Report per shape: restore-OK rate, full-reprocessing rate, mean/median tokens
  re-processed, and the effective usable prefix (cached tokens on the first
  completion after restore).
- Emit `results/<label>/invalidation.json` + markdown table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Invalidation table for the four restore shapes at each prompt size, with
  n >= 3 per cell: restore-OK rate, full-reprocessing rate, tokens re-processed
  (median/p90), effective usable prefix fraction.
- Requirement from `AGENTS.md` respected: `forcing full prompt re-processing` is
  reported as *expected hybrid-arch behaviour with a cost*, never as a defect —
  the table quantifies the cost, and the doc says so explicitly.
- The prefix-drift control behaves as expected (near-zero usable prefix); if it
  does not, the recording/attribution method is reported as unproven and the
  numbers are marked non-authoritative rather than published as fact.
- The one-turn-extension shape is measured, because it is the shape that decides
  whether virtual slots help real sessions (which always extend context).
- Log-marker attribution method is documented so another operator can reproduce
  the counts from the raw logs.

## Constraints

- llama-server logs carry no timestamps — attribution must use log byte offsets
  captured around each request, per the caveat in
  `docs/slot-persistence-analysis-harness.md`.
- Read-only access to `/var/log/llama-proxy/`; no log rewriting.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `scripts/slot_persistence_harness.py` (log-parsing reference)
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` (window-metric reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/invalidation.json` (new artifact)

# Measure memory and page-cache pressure for N=8 session snapshots

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 4.

## Target outcome

The resource cost of holding 8 session snapshots instead of 2: per-snapshot
footprint, bytes per token, aggregate on-disk and host page-cache growth at N=8,
and the system `MemAvailable` delta — with VRAM reported as non-available rather
than guessed, per the fidelity convention in
`docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode memory` in the harness: build N=8 distinct session prefixes, save all
  eight (bounded by free page cache), then measure:
  - on-disk size per snapshot and total (also reported by
    `du -sb` on the run's own directory);
  - `/proc/meminfo` `Cached` and `MemAvailable` before/after each save and after
    the full set, plus the page-cache residency of the snapshot files;
  - read-back bandwidth: sequential read of each snapshot to `/dev/null` (the
    proxy's restore path reads the whole file), giving MiB/s — the term that
    determines restore cost as snapshots grow.
- Derive bytes/token per size and extrapolate to N=8 for a realistic mix,
  stating the mix used.
- Record the ROCm VRAM reading and mark it explicitly non-available/ungraded
  (the known-degraded ~0.2 GB reading), instead of reporting a false number.
- Emit `results/<label>/memory.json` + markdown table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-size snapshot footprint and bytes/token, measured (not derived-only).
- N=8 aggregate footprint (sum of snapshot sizes) and observed `Cached` growth,
  with the delta between them explained (page cache vs. written-but-not-resident).
- `MemAvailable` delta across a full N=8 set, and the maximum resident footprint
  observed during the run.
- Read-back bandwidth (MiB/s) for snapshot files, which the verdict uses to
  extrapolate restore cost.
- VRAM is either measured credibly or explicitly reported as non-available with
  the reason; no estimated VRAM figure is presented as measured.
- The run cleans up the snapshots it created and reports the post-cleanup
  `MemAvailable` / `Cached` return-to-baseline.

## Constraints

- Must not fill the page cache to the point of harming live inference: the run
  is bounded by a `--max-write-mib` guard (default sized from current
  `MemAvailable`) and stops early, recording truncation.
- No `drop_caches` unless explicitly permitted by the operator; measure the
  natural page-cache behaviour instead.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py` (per-token KV expectation reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/memory.json` (new artifact)
- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`

# Harness-side virtual-slot prototype: 8 session slots over 2 physical slots

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 5 — the end-to-end contention
comparison. **Gated on OPEN QUESTION 2** (recorded on the parent): AC5 of the
spike asks for 8 virtual slots over 2 physical slots, but virtual slots do not
exist and must not be added to production. This child delivers the measurement
as a *harness-side prototype* unless the producer directs otherwise.

## Target outcome

A measured p50/p90 first-byte latency and throughput comparison between
(A) 2 logical sessions on 2 physical slots (today's baseline) and (B) 8 logical
sessions multiplexed onto 2 physical slots by swap-in/swap-out of KV snapshots,
using a synthetic 8-concurrent-session workload.

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/benchmarks/virtual_slot_prototype.py` (or a `--mode virtual` in the
  harness): an 8-entry session table mapping logical session → physical
  llama-server slot; on dispatch it restores the session's snapshot into a free
  physical slot (evicting the current occupant with a save first), issues the
  completion, then saves the session's snapshot back.
- Workload: 8 concurrent synthetic sessions, each doing K turns with a shared
  prefix and per-turn growth, sized from the spike's four prompt sizes; turn
  gaps chosen to force real evictions.
- Metrics per configuration: TTFT p50/p90, per-session abandon count (requests
  that could not get a physical slot within the configured queue budget — the
  harness's analogue of `fallback_after_queue`), save/restore counts and
  failures, restored-hit rate, and completion count.
- Both configurations run back-to-back in one invocation so drift is shared.
- Emit `results/<label>/contention.json` + markdown table with an explicit
  A/B delta column.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A/B table for N_logical = 2 (baseline) vs N_logical = 8 over 2 physical slots:
  TTFT p50/p90, throughput, abandon count, save/restore counts, hit-rate,
  per-configuration duration.
- The eviction cost is counted, not hidden: for every restore that displaces
  another session, the displaced session's next-turn cold cost is measured and
  reported (this is the "eviction cost it imposes" term the parent requires).
- The run states plainly whether the prototype is a faithful model of a
  production virtual-slot implementation, listing the differences (no proxy
  routing, no dispatch leases, no contention queue) — no implied production
  parity.
- If 8-over-2 cannot complete within a bounded budget (e.g. wall-clock cap), the
  partial result is reported with the completion fraction rather than being
  silently truncated.
- The prototype lives only under `proxy/benchmarks/`; a test/documentation
  assertion confirms no production module is imported for dispatch.

## Constraints

- No production behaviour change (parent AC5).
- Must not starve live sessions: the run requires a quiet window or an explicit
  recorded validity caveat, mirroring
  `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` § `Fidelity caveats`.

## Risks

- Two prior live sweeps failed under concurrent load (600-760 s stalls,
  llama-server health probes unanswered). If the quiet window cannot be obtained,
  this child must fall back to the analytic model in the verdict child and say
  so — do not retry the live run indefinitely.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` (concurrency/sweep reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_simulation.py` (queue-model reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/contention.json` (new artifact)

# Results doc: tables, break-even model, go/no-go verdict and substitutes

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Satisfies AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC5 of the spike.

## Target outcome

A committed document `docs/virtual-slot-spike-LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE.md` containing
the complete measured tables, an explicit break-even inequality, a go/no-go
verdict, and — if not viable — the cheaper substitutes ranked with the measured
evidence for each.

## Minimal implementation

- Assemble the tables from the four measurement children's JSON artifacts
  (save size/time, restore time, restore hit-rate, invalidated-restore rate,
  memory delta, contention A/B). Cross-link each number to its result file and
  commit so the doc is auditable, not just descriptive.
- Break-even model, stated as an inequality with every term measured:
  `hit_rate × (cold_prefill_s − restore_s) > (1 − hit_rate) × eviction_reprefill_s + save_s_share`
  — or an equivalent explicit form — with the measured values substituted and
  the resulting break-even `hit_rate*` solved for each prompt size. State the
  cold-prefill baseline used (window median 61.8 s dispatch-first-byte, p90
  269.8 s) and the solitary cold-prefill figures from the parent's impact
  analysis (~254 new tok/s).
- Verdict: `go` (build virtual slots) / `no-go` (not viable) / `conditional`
  (viable only under a named condition), each with the driving measurement
  quoted. If `no-go`, rank the substitutes with measured evidence:
  more physical slots (LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8 — keep N=2 pending
  LP-0MVGPEP3O000RKKD), idle-aware admission (LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J implementation
  done; LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD / LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF measurement), shorter
  post-stream lease (locate and cite the owning item).
- Fidelity section reproducing the caveat conventions
  (`docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`): what could not be measured,
  VRAM non-availability, and the live-load validity caveat if applicable.
- AC5 proof: a `No production behaviour change` section listing the commits
  touched (`git diff --stat` restricted to `proxy/benchmarks/`, `proxy/tests/`,

## Summary

A zero-value artefact is tracked in the repository: a file literally named `=` at the repo root, whose content is a JSON dump of work item `LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR` (2394 bytes). It was committed by a bulk "pending working-tree changes" commit (`187cc857`) and is present in `dev`, `main`, `origin/dev` and `origin/main`. Remove it, and add a cheap regression guard so a shell-redirection typo (`cmd > =`) can never be committed again.

## Problem statement

A stray tracked file named `=` at the repo root is committed on `dev` and `main`. It is dead weight in every clone and every worktree, and it is a symptom of redirect-typo artefacts reaching the shared branches unreviewed — the same class of leak as the previously removed `node_modules` symlink and `.implement_state.json`.

## Users

- **Repository maintainers / release operators** — need a clean tracked-file surface so `git status`, audits, and release diffs stay meaningful.
- **AI agents working in worktrees** — a tracked junk file risks being "restored to HEAD" or re-committed by `git add -A` during implement runs.

Example user stories:

- As a release operator, I want `git ls-files` at the repo root to list only intentional files, so that audits and diffs are not polluted by agent-tooling debris.
- As a maintainer, I want a failing test (not tribal knowledge) to catch a future redirect-typo file, so that recurrence is caught before it reaches `dev`.

## Existing state

- `git ls-files --error-unmatch '='` succeeds; `git ls-tree` shows the file on `dev`, `main`, `origin/dev`, `origin/main`.
- Content is a JSON dump of work item `LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR` — evidence of a `wl show … > =` style redirect typo (the intended target was likely `>` or `=` was meant to be a variable name).
- Committed in `187cc857` ("chore: commit pending working-tree changes (AGENTS.md trim, stray wl export file)").
- Existing precedent for this class of fix: `LP-0MSI3XN6P005RO9U` (tracked `.implement_state.json` removal) and `tests/test_no_tracked_dependency_symlinks.py` (regression guard for tracked `node_modules` paths).
- No `.gitignore` rule covers shell-operator filenames today.

## Desired change

1. `git rm '='` on a feature branch and merge to `dev`; the file disappears from `main` automatically at the next `dev`→`main` release (ship skill), so no direct `main` commit is needed.
2. Add a narrow regression guard in the existing test suite that fails if a tracked path is a bare shell-redirection artefact (e.g. a repo-root filename composed only of `=`, `>`, `>>`, `|`, `<` characters, or other shell-operator-only names), with an explicit assertion that `=` is untracked. Model it on `tests/test_no_tracked_dependency_symlinks.py` (uses `git ls-files` against the live git state).
3. Deliberately **not** in scope: a `.gitignore` entry for `=` (would hide the artefact instead of failing loudly) and any change to `.githooks/pre-push` (adding a shell-level gate would require updating `tests/test_git_hooks.py` and duplicates what the pytest guard already achieves at the same dev-push gate).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git ls-files --error-unmatch '='` fails (file no longer tracked) on `dev` after merge.
- [ ] Working tree no longer contains a repo-root file named `=` (`test ! -e =`), and `git status --porcelain` shows no untracked `=` residue or stray stash left behind.
- [ ] A new regression test asserts no tracked bare shell-operator filename exists at the repo root **and** that `=` specifically is untracked; the test fails if the file is re-added (`git add --intent-to-add`/re-commit simulation verified by temporarily re-adding in a scratch clone or by unit-testing the detection helper).
- [ ] The removal commit is a scoped `chore` commit — no unrelated files, no behavioural code change.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — or explicitly confirmed as N/A (no doc or comment references tracked root artefacts).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Push to `dev` only; never commit directly to `main` (the release pipeline promotes `dev`→`main`).
- Keep the change surgical: one deletion plus one small, self-contained test file; no refactoring of nearby tests.
- `git add -A` in agent flows must not resurrect the file — the removal must be committed properly, not merely deleted locally.
- Respect repository boundaries: no edits to `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/`, or agent-infrastructure directories.

## Out of scope

- Broader repo-root tidy-up (e.g. the other one-off root artefacts such as `benchmark-qwen3*.json`, `eval*-report.md`) — different provenance; raise separately if wanted.
- Making the shared `implement`/worklog tooling refuse to write redirect targets — upstream framework concern, not this repo.

## Key Files

- `=` — delete; stray tracked file (JSON dump of `LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR`).
- `tests/test_no_stray_root_artifacts.py` — new regression guard, modelled on `tests/test_no_tracked_dependency_symlinks.py`.
- `tests/test_no_tracked_dependency_symlinks.py` — reference implementation / style precedent (no changes required).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the `=` file may still be reachable in `main` if the next release is delayed → mitigated by the fact that the removal rides the normal `dev`→`main` promotion; no separate `main` hotfix is warranted for a zero-impact hygiene artefact.
- **Risk:** a generic shell-operator test could false-positive on legitimate files → mitigated by restricting the guard to shell-operator-only filenames and to the repo root.
- **Risk:** scope creep into general root-file curation → explicitly out of scope (see above).
- **Assumption:** the file has no consumers (`grep` shows no references to a root file named `=`), so removal is behaviourally inert.
- **Assumption (documented, not confirmed by the producer):** a pytest regression guard is the preferred guard form over a hook or `.gitignore` rule, matching the `node_modules` precedent.

## Related work

- `LP-0MSI3XN6P005RO9U` — Remove stale tracked `.implement_state.json` from repo root (completed) — direct precedent for this class of fix.
- `LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR` — the work item whose JSON export leaked into the stray file (source of the artefact, not itself defective).
- `LP-0MVK0969J004MTG3` — discoverer item (`discovered-from`).
- `tests/test_no_tracked_dependency_symlinks.py` — precedent regression guard for tracked-path hygiene.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No operator interview was required: the seed context (originating from the repo inspection recorded in `LP-0MVK0969J004MTG3`) already identified the exact file, its provenance (`187cc857`), its presence on all four branches, and the intended action. Repo-first research answered the remaining questions:

- Q: "Is the file referenced anywhere (tests, scripts, docs, packaging)?" — Answer (agent, repo research): No — `git ls-files` root listing plus `grep` show no consumer; it is an orphaned redirect artefact. Source: `git show --stat 187cc857`, repo-wide `grep`.
- Q: "Does a precedent exist for removing tracked junk and guarding against recurrence?" — Answer (agent, repo research): Yes — `LP-0MSI3XN6P005RO9U` (`.implement_state.json`, `git rm` + verify) and `tests/test_no_tracked_dependency_symlinks.py` (`git ls-files` guard). Source: worklog search, file inspection.
- Q: "Is the file also on `main`, requiring a hotfix?" — Answer (agent, repo research): Yes on `main`, but the `dev`→`main` release promotion carries the removal, so no direct `main` commit is required. Source: `git ls-tree dev|main|origin/dev|origin/main -- '='`.
- Q: "Which guard form: pytest test, pre-push hook, or `.gitignore` rule?" — Answer (agent, documented assumption): pytest regression test at repo root scope; `.gitignore` would silently hide the artefact and a hook change would duplicate the dev-push gate while requiring `tests/test_git_hooks.py` updates. Flagged for producer confirmation.

# Intake brief — Slot-sweep harness cannot exercise local concurrency: add a warm-start / staggered-arrival mode

**Headline:** Make the slot-sweep harness land requests on the local backend under concurrency by adding a warm-start priming gate (proves `cold_start.is_cold() == False` via a completed local prefill) plus a configurable `--stagger-seconds`, so N=2/N=3 runs report `local_stream_share > 0` with ≥2 concurrent local streams and auditable per-request resolved models.

## Problem statement

The controlled N=2/N=3 slot sweep (LP-0MVK096GF0038FTH) produced **local stream share 0.0%** at both counts: every completed benchmark stream was served by a remote provider, so no local TTFT/decode metrics exist and the concurrency-vs-capacity projection (N=2 denies ~19.7% of session-minutes, N=3 ~6.7%) is untestable with the harness as configured. The root cause is structural: each slot-count restart re-arms the proxy's cold-start admission window (`proxy/proxy/cold_start.py`, cap = 1 concurrent local dispatch until the first local prefill completes and calls `mark_warm`), and the harness launches `--concurrency N` inside that window. Because even the first request never completed a local prefill within the run (observed `backend busy (health check timeout)` for the whole window), `mark_warm` never fired and cold cap never lifted — so a fixed 60 s stagger (already present as `INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S`) did not and cannot fix it.

## Users

- **Producer / capacity owner** (rgardler/agents assessing `session_slot_pool_size`): needs a trustworthy N=2-vs-N=3 local-latency comparison to re-decide the slot count (reopening conditions in `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` depend on this item).
  - *User story:* "As a capacity owner, I want the slot sweep to exercise ≥2 concurrent local streams so the N=2-vs-N=3 decision is based on local TTFT/decode data, not remote fallback numbers."
- **Benchmark operator** (agent running the sweep in a quiet window): needs a single deterministic command that lands requests locally without manual heroics.
  - *User story:* "As a benchmark operator, I want one flag such as `--warm-start` plus `--stagger-seconds` so each slot-count cycle warms the local backend before the measured set launches, and I can read the local share from the report JSON."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The sweep harness gains a warm-start mode in which, after each slot-count restart, a short priming request is sent and must **complete locally** (`resolved_model` local, e.g. `local-qwen3/…`) — proving the first local prefill ran and `mark_warm` lifted the cold cap — before the measured request set is launched; the priming request is deliberately small (single turn, short prompt, e.g. `--test`'s 'Say Hi', ≤20 completion tokens) so it completes within the 1 200 s client timeout and the 120 s cold grace window; if the priming request cannot land locally within a bounded retry budget, the run fails fast with a clear error instead of silently falling back remote.
- [ ] A configurable `--stagger-seconds N` argument (default 0 = all-at-once) spaces the *measured* request starts as requested; the fixed `INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S` constant no longer silently forces a 60 s gap, and `--stagger-seconds 0` preserves the pre-existing all-at-once launch only when explicitly intended.
- [ ] A re-run of `--sweep --resume 2 --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000` (N=2 then N=3) reports `contention.local_stream_share > 0` with **at least 2 concurrent local streams observed**, and `slot_<N>.json` records per-request `resolved_model` so the local share is auditable.
- [ ] New tests cover the warm-start gate (priming must complete locally before measured launch; bounded-retry failure path aborts the run) and the stagger math (`--stagger-seconds N` → start deltas of `N` seconds); all existing tests pass.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs-site entries — specifically the new flags in `slot_benchmark.py --help`, the sweep RESULTS_NOTE, and the reopen-conditions doc (`docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md`).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Structural root cause is proxy-side and correct behaviour:** the cold-start cap (LP-0MUCEFCAT005NFNN) exists to protect a post-restart GPU from thundering-herd prefills; it must not be weakened or disabled in `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` for the benchmark's sake. The fix belongs in the harness (warm the backend before measuring) — or, if routed via proxy, must be opt-in and not alter the production cold-start guard.
- **Sweep lock / quiet-window constraints:** the run must still pass `scripts/slot_sweep_preflight.py` (quiet window, config unchanged, `session_slot_pool_size` restored after the sweep — AC5 of LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7).
- **Do not corrupt production state:** slot cache and prompt cache preserved by default (`--clean-cache` remains OFF); `proxy/config.yaml` restored in `finally`.
- **Client-timeout budget:** agentic turns target up to 18 000 output tokens (~600 s); priming must be a *small* request (e.g. "Say Hi" / minimal prompt) so it completes within the 1 200 s client timeout and the cold grace window (default 120 s).
- **No ad-hoc full-suite runs during implementation; all test invocations go through the test skill.**

## Existing state

- Harness: `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` — existing flags: `--sweep`, `--slots`, `--all`, `--test`, `--dry-run`, `--resume`, `--skip-restart`, `--warmup` (concurrent warmup task, **not** a gate), `--clean-cache`, `--phase`, `--concurrency`, `--prompt-tokens`, `--log-dir`, `--no-health-samples`. `INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S = 60.0` hard-codes a 60 s stagger inside `run_slot_benchmark`.
- Cold-start admission: `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` — `note_model_loaded()` arms the window on restart; `mark_warm()` lifts the cap on first data chunk (called from `proxy/proxy/router.py` and `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`); cap `effective_max_concurrent` defaults to 1 while cold.
- Local share metric: `derive_local_stream_share()` in `slot_benchmark.py` computes `local_stream_share` from per-request `resolved_model` (`X-Resolved-Model` response header); `is_local_resolved_model()` classifies `local-qwen3/…` as local.
- Evidence: `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/RESULTS_NOTE.md` (both runs INVALID, 0.0% local share, root-cause write-up) and `sweep_n2_n3.log` (request 1 stuck in `backend busy (health check timeout)` for the entire window).
- Verdict doc: `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` — re-open condition #1 is exactly this item.

## Desired change

Add to `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py`:

1. **Warm-start priming gate** (`--warm-start` flag or enabled by default in `--sweep` mode): after the restart + `Llama-server ready`, send one small priming request (short prompt, 1 turn) and poll its completion. Success = request completed with `is_local_resolved_model(resolved_model)` true (local prefill done ⇒ `mark_warm` fired). Only then create the measured request tasks. Bounded retry/timeout (e.g. re-send up to K times within the cold grace window); treat persistent failure as a run error with a diagnostic message (`cold_start.is_cold()` reference / `local_dispatch_denied` log lines), never a silent remote fallback.
2. **Configurable `--stagger-seconds N`** (default 0): replace the hard-coded `INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S * idx` delay with `stagger_seconds * idx`; keep the existing per-request concurrent-overlap semantics (requests still run concurrently once started). Default 0 preserves today's all-at-once launch for explicit use; the sweep invocation passes `--stagger-seconds 0` or a small value explicitly.
3. **Test mode compat:** `--test` ("Say Hi" connectivity check) still works and can double as the priming probe.

Design note (why the warm-start gate, not stagger alone): the 2026-10-23 log already had a 60 s stagger active, yet request 1 never completed a local prefill (`backend busy (health check timeout)`), so `mark_warm` never fired and all measured requests fell back remote. A stagger alone cannot fix a first-request-that-never-lands; only a gate that *proves* a local prefill completed before the measured set launches can. The priming request is also the only harness-visible proof of `cold_start.is_cold() == False` (the state is in-process, not exposed via `/health`).

## Key Files:

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` — add `--warm-start` gate + `--stagger-seconds`; rework `run_slot_benchmark` task creation (priming phase before measured set); replace `INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S` usage.
- `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` — **reference only** (do not weaken the guard); may warrant a `__main__`-adjacent probe or a comment cross-ref, not production changes.
- `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` — update re-open condition #1 evidence once a valid run lands.
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/RESULTS_NOTE.md` — reference/limitations; future valid-run results go in a new results dir.
- `tests/test_slot_benchmark_warm_start.py` — new unit tests for the priming gate + stagger math (follow existing harness-test conventions, e.g. `tests/test_slot_sweep_preflight.py`).
- `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` — document the new `--warm-start` / `--stagger-seconds` flags (AC5) and the default-0 stagger (INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S removed).

## Related work

- `LP-0MVK09622002CRMR` — Record slot-count verdict and reconcile with projection (discovered-from source; held verdict awaiting this item).
- `LP-0MVK096GF0038FTH` — Execute N=2/N=3/N=4 slot sweep in a quiet window (produced the INVALID 0.0%-local-share results).
- `LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7` — Slot sweep 1/2/3 with recorded results (AC5 config-drift guard).
- `LP-0MUCEFCAT005NFNN` — Cold-start admission control (proxy mechanism being worked around).
- `LP-0MVLHNJ3W007T319` — slot_benchmark: record finish_reason per request (related harness gap; listed in reopen doc as a precondition).
- `LP-0MRWUAXRX004JZSO` — Add staggered start support to run_benchmark.py (precedent for `--stagger` flag in the sibling harness `run_benchmark.py`).
- `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md`, `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/RESULTS_NOTE.md` — decision + evidence docs.

## Assumptions & risks

- **Assumption (design choice):** implement the **warm-start priming gate** as the primary fix (description: "any one is enough"), with `--stagger-seconds` as a complementary control. Rationale: the 60 s stagger already present was proven insufficient in the 2026-10-23 log. Recorded in the Appendix; producer may override at review (alternative: stagger-only, or single-turn production-sized requests).
- **Risk — priming request could also be denied** if llama-server is still settling (observed `backend busy (health check timeout)`): mitigate with bounded retries within the grace window and fail-fast diagnostic on persistent failure; do NOT measure 0.0%-local-share as a valid result.
- **Risk — valid-run scope creep:** a successful sweep re-run (this item's goal) may invite re-deciding slot count (LP-0MVK09622002CRMR verdict) — that is a separate review decision, out of scope here; record as follow-up, not scope.
- **Risk — warm-start hides cold-start behaviour:** the gate intentionally measures *warm* concurrency only (matches production: sessions arrive staggered and warm); cold-start behaviour stays the proxy's domain and is not what this sweep evaluates.
- **Risk — auditability:** local share is derived from `X-Resolved-Model` headers; ensure priming request and measured requests record `resolved_model` so the share is provable.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview was conducted: this item was auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker (headless, no operator present), and the seed description is exceptionally detailed (root cause, three accepted capabilities, embedded draft AC, and explicit "any one is enough" discretion). The design decision below is therefore recorded as a research-backed assumption for producer review rather than an interactive answer.

- Q (design decision — routed to producer for confirmation at review): "Which of the three accepted capabilities should this item implement — `--stagger-seconds N`, a warm-start priming gate, or single-turn production-sized requests?" — **Recommended:** warm-start priming gate + configurable `--stagger-seconds` — a fixed stagger alone is proven insufficient by the 2026-10-23 log (60 s stagger active, yet request 1 never completed a local prefill, so `mark_warm` never fired); the gate is the only harness-visible proof of `is_cold() == False`. Answer (Map): assumption recorded 2026-10-24; no interactive answer available (headless dispatch). Source: `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/sweep_n2_n3.log` (staggered starts at 21:08:29/21:09:29/21:10:29 with request 1 stuck in `backend busy (health check timeout)`), `RESULTS_NOTE.md` ("Why local share is 0 %"), `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` (`INTER_REQUEST_GAP_S = 60.0`).
- Q (scope): "Should the proxy's cold-start cap be changed to make the sweep pass?" — Answer (research): **No.** The cap (LP-0MUCEFCAT005NFNN) protects the GPU from post-restart prefill floods in production; weakening it is out of scope and would corrupt the very behaviour the projection models. Fix belongs in the harness. Source: `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` docstring.

Duplicate-work check performed: `wl search "slot sweep"` / `"warm-start"` / `"stagger"` — no overlapping open item found; `LP-0MRWUAXRX004JZSO` (run_benchmark.py `--stagger`) is completed and targets the sibling harness, not `slot_benchmark.py` — noted as related precedent, not a duplicate.
